meta.subject: DATA_SCIENCE
meta.author: bank-team-data-science
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.learningObjective: Identify rows above their group average
questions.stem: Clerk Ana compares each case's hours to its department average; which rows qualify?

options.text: Rows whose hours exceed their department average
Rows whose hours exceed the global average
options.misconception: uses global instead of group average

options.text: Rows with the maximum hours overall

questions.explanation: A row qualifies when its value exceeds its own group average, not the global average.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a correlated subquery result
questions.stem: Clerk Ben runs a correlated subquery returning department average per case; what does each outer row receive?

options.text: The overall average across all cases

questions.explanation: Correlation ties the subquery to the outer row's department, so each case gets its department average.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.learningObjective: Explain a running total at frame end
questions.stem: Clerk Chen computes running total of case fees through each month; value at last row?

answer.exemplar: The running total at the last row equals the sum of all case fees across every month in the partition, since the frame includes all preceding rows.

questions.explanation: At the last row the frame includes all preceding rows, so the running total equals the full sum.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.learningObjective: Apply dense rank to tied values
questions.stem: Three cases tie for first by fee; dense rank of the next case?
questions.explanation: Dense rank assigns consecutive ranks, so after a tie at first the next case gets rank 2.

questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie
questions.learningObjective: Handle top two per group with ties
questions.stem: Clerk wants top 2 cases per department by fee, including ties; which function?
questions.explanation: RANK includes ties, so filtering rank <= 2 keeps top 2 including tied rows.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.learningObjective: Count rows a recursive walk produces
questions.stem: Recursive walk of a case chain starting at 1 row with 2 children each level for 3 levels; total rows?
questions.explanation: A binary tree 3 levels deep has 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 nodes including root.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.learningObjective: Identify seekable queries for a composite index
questions.stem: Composite index on (department, status); which query can seek?
questions.explanation: A composite index seeks when the query filters on the leading column and optionally the next.

questions.topic: Inner rows a nested-loop join reads
questions.learningObjective: Count inner rows a nested loop reads
questions.stem: Nested loop join: outer 10 rows, inner 5 rows each; how many inner reads?

answer.exemplar: The nested loop reads 50 inner rows because 10 outer iterations each scan all 5 inner rows, totalling 50 reads.

questions.explanation: Nested loop reads inner rows once per outer row: 10 times 5 equals 50.

questions.topic: Rows produced by a lost join condition
questions.learningObjective: Identify rows from a lost join condition
questions.stem: Join loses its condition and becomes a cross join: 12 cases times 5 departments; rows produced?
questions.explanation: A cross join produces the Cartesian product: 12 times 5 equals 60 rows.

questions.topic: Rows an offset page repeats
questions.learningObjective: Identify repeated rows across offset pages
questions.stem: Clerk pages cases with OFFSET 10 LIMIT 10 then OFFSET 15 LIMIT 10; what repeats?

options.text: Rows 16 through 20 appear in both pages

questions.explanation: Offsets 10 and 15 overlap on rows 16-20, so those rows appear in both pages.

questions.topic: Queries a repeated lookup issues
questions.learningObjective: Count queries from a repeated lookup
questions.stem: N+1 problem: 1 query for 50 cases plus 1 per case; total queries?
questions.explanation: One initial query plus 50 per-case queries totals 51 queries.

questions.topic: Distinct entities behind duplicated links
questions.learningObjective: Count distinct entities behind duplicated links
questions.stem: 100 link rows but only 30 distinct cases; how many distinct entities?
questions.explanation: Distinct entities are counted by unique case, so 30 distinct cases remain.

questions.topic: A cost claim against the plan
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a cost claim against a plan
questions.stem: Clerk claims an index scan is cheaper than a seq scan; plan shows seq scan chosen. Who is right?

answer.exemplar: The planner is right because it chose the seq scan based on cost estimates; the clerk's claim may ignore selectivity or table size factors.

questions.explanation: The planner picks the lower estimated cost, so its seq scan choice reflects its cost model.

questions.topic: Duplicate share of a multiplied result
questions.learningObjective: Compute duplicate share of a multiplied result
questions.stem: Result has 100 rows, 40 are duplicates of existing cases; duplicate share percent?
questions.explanation: Duplicate share is 40 out of 100, or 40 percent.

questions.topic: Reading a plan for a table scan
questions.learningObjective: Read a plan for a table scan
questions.stem: Plan shows Seq Scan on cases; what does it imply?

options.misconception: confuses seq scan with index scan

options.text: Every row of cases is read

questions.explanation: A sequential scan reads every row of the table.

questions.topic: An index that a query cannot use
questions.learningObjective: Identify an unusable index
questions.stem: Query filters WHERE LOWER(name) = 'smith'; index on name. Can it be used?

options.text: No, function on column prevents index use

questions.explanation: Wrapping a column in a function prevents a plain index on that column from being used.

questions.topic: A join result larger than both inputs
questions.learningObjective: Explain a join larger than both inputs
questions.stem: Join of 10 cases and 10 departments yields 40 rows; why larger than inputs?

options.misconception: outer join size bounded by sum

questions.explanation: Shared join keys cause multiplication, producing more rows than either input.

questions.topic: Reading a composite index order
questions.learningObjective: Read composite index column order
questions.stem: Composite index on (department, status, date); which column must lead for a seek?

answer.exemplar: The leading column department must be filtered with equality for the index to seek; without it the index cannot be used efficiently.

questions.explanation: The leading column must be constrained for a composite index seek to occur.

questions.topic: Reading duplicated rows across pages
questions.learningObjective: Read duplicated rows across pages
questions.stem: Page size 10, overlap of 5 rows between consecutive pages; distinct rows in 2 pages?
questions.explanation: Two pages of 10 with 5 overlap yield 10 + 10 - 5 = 15 distinct rows.

questions.topic: Reading a running-total series
questions.learningObjective: Read a running-total series
questions.stem: Running totals: 10, 25, 40; what was the third increment?
questions.explanation: Third increment is 40 minus 25 equals 15.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.learningObjective: Apply group average filter
questions.stem: Clerk flags cases above their department average; which SQL pattern?
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery computes the department average for comparison.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate correlated subquery cost
questions.stem: Correlated subquery on 10000 cases; performance concern?

options.text: It executes once per outer row

questions.explanation: Correlation causes per-row execution, which is costly for large tables.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.learningObjective: Apply running total frame
questions.stem: Clerk needs running total of fees ordered by date; frame?

answer.exemplar: Use SUM(fee) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) to accumulate fees through each date.

questions.explanation: Unbounded preceding to current row accumulates all prior fees plus current.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate dense rank with multiple ties
questions.stem: Values: 10,10,10,8; dense rank of 8?
questions.explanation: Three ties at rank 1, so value 8 gets dense rank 2.

questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate top two with tie inclusion
questions.stem: Top 2 per department using RANK; department has 3 tied at first. How many rows?
questions.explanation: RANK gives all three tied rows rank 1, and rank <= 2 includes them; rank 2 row would also be included if present, but here only 3 ties.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.learningObjective: Apply recursive walk to a hierarchy
questions.stem: Recursive walk of employee hierarchy from manager down; which rows produced?

options.text: Manager and all direct and indirect reports

questions.explanation: Recursive walk traverses the entire hierarchy from the manager downward.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate composite index seekability
questions.stem: Index on (department, status); query WHERE status = 'open' AND department = 'A'. Seekable?
questions.explanation: Both leading and second columns are constrained, so the index can seek.

questions.topic: Inner rows a nested-loop join reads
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate nested loop read count
questions.stem: Nested loop: outer 20, inner 8 each; clerk says 28 reads. Correct?

answer.exemplar: No, the correct count is 160 reads because 20 outer rows times 8 inner rows equals 160, not 28.

questions.explanation: Nested loop reads 20 times 8 equals 160 inner rows, not 28.

questions.topic: Rows produced by a lost join condition
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate lost join condition impact
questions.stem: Lost condition turns join into cross join: 5 cases, 4 departments. Rows?
questions.explanation: Cross join produces 5 times 4 equals 20 rows.

questions.topic: Rows an offset page repeats
questions.learningObjective: Create a page with no repeat
questions.stem: Clerk wants no repeated rows across pages; which approach?

options.text: Use DISTINCT in the page query
Use keyset pagination on a unique column

questions.explanation: Keyset pagination on a unique column avoids overlap between pages.

questions.topic: Queries a repeated lookup issues
questions.learningObjective: Create a query avoiding N+1
questions.stem: Clerk wants to avoid N+1 when loading cases with departments; best approach?

options.text: Use a join or eager fetch in one query

questions.explanation: A single join or eager fetch retrieves all data in one query, avoiding N+1.

questions.topic: Distinct entities behind duplicated links
questions.learningObjective: Create a deduplicated entity list
questions.stem: Clerk wants one row per distinct case from duplicated links; which query?
questions.explanation: DISTINCT collapses duplicated links to one row per case.

questions.topic: A cost claim against the plan
questions.learningObjective: Create an index to support a claim
questions.stem: Clerk claims an index would speed a filter; what must be verified first?

answer.exemplar: Verify the filter column has sufficient selectivity and that the query's cost estimate favors an index scan over a sequential scan.

questions.explanation: An index helps only if selectivity and cost estimates favor it over a seq scan.

questions.topic: Duplicate share of a multiplied result
questions.learningObjective: Create a deduplication to reduce duplicate share
questions.stem: Duplicate share 40% of 100 rows; after dedup to 60 distinct rows, new duplicate share?
questions.explanation: After deduplication no duplicates remain, so duplicate share is 0 percent.

questions.topic: Reading a plan for a table scan
questions.learningObjective: Create an index to avoid a seq scan
questions.stem: Plan shows Seq Scan; clerk wants index scan; what to add?

options.text: An index on the filtered column

questions.explanation: An index on the filtered column lets the planner choose an index scan.

questions.topic: An index that a query cannot use
questions.learningObjective: Create a usable index for a function filter
questions.stem: Query filters WHERE LOWER(name) = 'smith'; best index?
questions.explanation: An expression index on LOWER(name) matches the filter function.

questions.topic: A join result larger than both inputs
questions.learningObjective: Create a join without multiplication
questions.stem: Clerk wants join result no larger than inputs; which condition?

options.text: Join on unique keys in both tables

questions.explanation: Joining on unique keys prevents row multiplication, keeping result size bounded.

questions.topic: Reading a composite index order
questions.learningObjective: Create an index matching query order
questions.stem: Query filters department then status then date; best composite index?

answer.exemplar: Create the index as (department, status, date) so column order matches the query's filter order from most to least selective.

questions.explanation: Index column order should match filter order for efficient seeking.

questions.topic: Reading duplicated rows across pages
questions.learningObjective: Create stable pagination without duplicates
questions.stem: Page size 20; keyset pagination on unique id avoids overlap; duplicates per page?
questions.explanation: Keyset pagination on a unique id produces no duplicate rows across pages.

questions.topic: Reading a running-total series
questions.learningObjective: Create a running total with reset per group
questions.stem: Clerk needs running total of fees per department, resetting each department; which query?

options.text: SUM(fee) OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY date)

questions.explanation: Partition by department resets the running total for each department.

questions.topic: Rows above their own group average
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate row count above group average
questions.stem: 10 cases, group averages vary; can all 10 be above their group average?

options.text: No, exactly half must be below
No, at least one must be at or below average

questions.explanation: By definition of average, not all values can exceed their group average.

questions.topic: Evaluations of a correlated subquery
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate correlated subquery with no match
questions.stem: Correlated subquery returns no rows for an outer row; what value?
questions.explanation: A scalar subquery returning no rows yields null.

questions.topic: Running total at the end of a frame
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate running total at frame boundary
questions.stem: Running total with frame ROWS 2 PRECEDING; value at first row of partition?

answer.exemplar: At the first row the frame contains only that row because there are no preceding rows, so the running total equals the first row's value.

questions.explanation: At the partition start, preceding rows do not exist, so the frame holds only the current row.

questions.topic: Dense rank across a tie
questions.learningObjective: Evaluate dense rank versus rank
questions.stem: Values: 5,5,4; RANK of 4 minus DENSE_RANK of 4?
questions.explanation: RANK of 4 is 3, DENSE_RANK of 4 is 2, difference is 1.

questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie
questions.learningObjective: Create top two per group without ties
questions.stem: Clerk wants exactly 2 rows per department, no ties; which function?

options.text: ROW_NUMBER partitioned by department ordered by fee desc

questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER assigns unique ranks, so filtering <= 2 yields exactly 2 rows per department.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.learningObjective: Create a recursive walk with cycle guard
questions.stem: Recursive walk on a graph with cycles; risk and fix?
questions.explanation: Cycles cause infinite recursion unless visited nodes are tracked.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.learningObjective: Create a composite index for multi-column filter
questions.stem: Query filters department = 'A' AND status = 'open' AND date > '2024-01-01'; best index?

options.misconception: date range first blocks seek on others

questions.explanation: Equality columns first then range column lets the index seek efficiently.

questions.topic: Inner rows a nested-loop join reads
questions.learningObjective: Create an index to reduce nested loop reads
questions.stem: Nested loop reads 1000 inner rows; how to reduce?

answer.exemplar: Add an index on the inner table's join column so each outer row seeks one inner row instead of scanning all rows.

questions.explanation: An index on the inner join column turns full scans into single-row seeks.

questions.topic: Rows produced by a lost join condition
questions.learningObjective: Create a guard against lost join condition
questions.stem: Code review catches a join with no ON clause; tables 10 and 10 rows. Rows if run?
questions.explanation: Missing ON makes a cross join: 10 times 10 equals 100 rows.

questions.topic: Rows an offset page repeats
questions.learningObjective: Create a deduplicated page result
questions.stem: Overlapping pages produce duplicate rows; clerk wants unique rows across all pages; approach?

options.text: Collect all then DISTINCT, or use keyset pagination

questions.explanation: DISTINCT after collection or keyset pagination eliminates cross-page duplicates.

questions.topic: Queries a repeated lookup issues
questions.learningObjective: Create a batched lookup
questions.stem: Clerk batches 50 case lookups into one query; queries issued?
questions.explanation: A single query with an IN list batches all 50 lookups into one round trip.

questions.topic: Distinct entities behind duplicated links
questions.learningObjective: Create a count of distinct entities
questions.stem: Clerk wants count of distinct cases in links; which query?
questions.explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT case_id) counts unique cases.

questions.topic: A cost claim against the plan
questions.learningObjective: Create a verified cost comparison
questions.stem: Clerk claims index is cheaper; how to verify against the plan?

answer.exemplar: Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on both plans and compare actual execution times and row counts to verify which is cheaper.

questions.explanation: EXPLAIN ANALYZE measures actual costs, validating or refuting the claim.

questions.topic: Duplicate share of a multiplied result
questions.learningObjective: Create a check for duplicate share threshold
questions.stem: Result 200 rows, 50 duplicates; duplicate share percent?
questions.explanation: 50 duplicates out of 200 rows is 25 percent.

questions.topic: Reading a plan for a table scan
questions.learningObjective: Create a covering index to avoid heap fetches
questions.stem: Plan shows index scan with heap fetches; clerk wants index-only scan; fix?

options.text: Include needed columns in the index

questions.explanation: Including all needed columns makes the index covering, enabling index-only scans.

questions.topic: An index that a query cannot use
questions.learningObjective: Create an index for a LIKE prefix query
questions.stem: Query filters WHERE name LIKE 'Sm%'; best index?

options.text: Plain index on name supports prefix seek

questions.explanation: A plain index supports prefix LIKE seeks.

questions.topic: A join result larger than both inputs
questions.learningObjective: Create a join on unique keys
questions.stem: Clerk joins cases to departments on department_id where both are unique; result size?

options.text: At most the number of cases

questions.explanation: Joining on unique keys prevents multiplication, so result is at most the case count.

questions.topic: Reading a composite index order
questions.learningObjective: Create an index for a query with range on first column
questions.stem: Query filters date range then department equality; can a composite index seek both?

answer.exemplar: No, once the first index column has a range condition the subsequent columns cannot be used for seeking, only filtering.

questions.explanation: A range on the leading column prevents seeking on later columns.

questions.topic: Reading duplicated rows across pages
questions.learningObjective: Create a count of distinct rows across pages
questions.stem: Two pages of 10 with 5 overlap; distinct rows total?
questions.explanation: Distinct rows across two overlapping pages: 10 + 10 - 5 = 15.

questions.topic: Reading a running-total series
questions.learningObjective: Create a running total with a moving window
questions.stem: Clerk wants 3-row moving sum of fees; which frame?

options.text: ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING
ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW

questions.explanation: Two preceding plus current row gives a 3-row moving sum.
